The chart effectively highlights the reduction in tourist engagement at each step, with 2009 consistently showing lower absolute numbers but similar proportional drop-offs compared to 2008. The clean, white background and distinct color contrast make it easy to compare the two years at a glance. source = '''import csv
import plotly.graph_objects as go

with open("table.csv", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))

data = {
    "Stage": [row["Stage"] for row in rows],
    "2008": [int(row["2008_Value"]) for row in rows],
    "2009": [int(row["2009_Value"]) for row in rows],
}

fig = go.Figure()

for year, color in [("2008", "#3498db"), ("2009", "#e74c3c")]:
    fig.add_trace(go.Funnel(
        name=year,
        y=data["Stage"],
        x=data[year],
        marker=dict(color=color),
        text=[f'{int(row[year + "_Value"]):,} ({row[year + "_Percent_Initial"]})'
              for row in rows],
        textinfo="text",
        textposition="inside",
        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x}<extra></extra>"
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Tourist Booking Funnel in Spain (2008 vs 2009)",
    funnelgap=0.1,
    plot_bgcolor='white',
    font=dict(size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1)
)

fig.write_image("output.png")
'''
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
print("Trace verification:", [(t.type, t.name, list(t.x), t.marker.color) for t in fig.data])
print("Layout:", fig.layout.title.text, fig.layout.font.size, fig.layout.legend)

            x=side * half_width, y=row["Stage"],
            xref="x", yref="y",
            text=f'{int(row[year + "_Value"]):,} ({row[year + "_Percent_Initial"]})',
            showarrow=False,
            xanchor="right" if side == -1 else "left",
            xshift=side * 5,
            font=dict(size=12)
        )

fig.write_image("output.png")
''')
